rubrics.criterion: The one-shot synchronous execution helpers are declared against capability-scoped contracts matching their bodies: the Exec-only helper (formerly ExecWith(db BaseRunner)) accepts a value that must supply only Exec, and the Query-only helper (formerly QueryWith(db BaseRunner)) accepts a value that must supply only Query; the sibling synchronous capability is no longer required at either seam.
rubrics.rationale: Both helper bodies invoke exactly one method on their parameter, and this case's injection deliberately fattened exactly these two parameters to a shared two-method shape; a repair that still requires the unused sibling capability at either seam has not resolved that cluster.

rubrics.criterion: Each of the three context execution helpers (ExecContextWith, QueryContextWith, QueryRowContextWith) is declared against a contract requiring only the single context capability that helper invokes, whether via the restored per-capability declarations or newly introduced focused ones; none of the three parameters references the fused synchronous-plus-context surface nor requires any synchronous capability.
rubrics.rationale: The homogenized context trio is this task's dominant cluster: three distinct seams were fattened to the same six-method surface while each body exercises exactly one method, so all three parameters must be narrowed for the cluster to count as resolved.

rubrics.criterion: The statement cache's dependency contracts are prepare-scoped: the cache's stored field (StmtCache.prep) and both constructor parameters (NewStmtCache, NewStmtCacher) accept values that must supply only Prepare and PrepareContext, and no execution capability is demanded of the cache's preparation target; equivalently shaped prepare-only declarations (one interface, or two split by context) both satisfy this.
rubrics.rationale: This package's cache code invokes only the prepare pair on its preparation target, yet the injection shoved the whole execution surface onto the cache's field and constructors; the cache cluster is resolved only when every one of those dependency points requires just the prepare capabilities.

rubrics.criterion: The public placeholder-format seam requires only ReplacePlaceholders for statement rendering: a replacement-only implementation assigns without error to every statement-data renderer's format field (selectData, insertData, updateData, deleteData), and no field or parameter behind ordinary statement rendering carries a debug/format-token obligation. Narrowing the public declaration, or re-typing the renderer fields to a replacement-only declaration, both satisfy this. Implementations that keep a debug token method (for the debug renderer's own discovery) remain allowed but must not be demanded by the rendering seam.
rubrics.rationale: The debug-token method was folded into the public placeholder contract during the injection, so four untouched statement-data structs silently carried an obligation their ToSql paths never call; the cluster is resolved however the repair restores replacement-only typing at the rendering dependency points.

rubrics.criterion: The narrowing is structurally real: the focused capability declarations the repair produces are exactly what the seam dependency points reference, and no dependency point in the runner/placeholder seam area still keeps a merged-surface or family-group declaration as its required type.
rubrics.rationale: This case's injection kept compatibility names alive by re-declaring them as the unified surface, so an alias-keeping repair that defines narrow contracts but leaves parameters and fields typed against the merged surface would compile and still carry the smell; this item pins the actual dependency-boundary repair rather than its paperwork.

rubrics.criterion: Standard-library database targets keep connecting end-to-end: a plain *sql.DB (or equivalent standard-shaped value) flows through the wrapper helpers and into the statement cache without being required to carry either the merged surface or any capability beyond those database/sql itself defines, and the seam migration covers every call site the re-split touched (wrapper construction, proxy wiring, cache plumbing, helper bodies) with no caller left passing or demanding the merged surface.
rubrics.rationale: The injection reinforced its widened cache constructors by pushing the wrapper (and prepare methods onto the standard-target interface StdSqlCtx) and hard-coding the wrapper at the proxy call site, so a coherent repair must reconcile this glue rather than leave a second seam half-migrated; this coupled consequence is specific to how this wave was stitched together.

rubrics.criterion: The statement cache's external availability is intact after the re-split: NewStmtCacheProxy still returns a proxy usable wherever a drop-in caching database target is wanted, its Begin path still begins a transaction by delegating to the underlying database handle (possibly through the re-split's own wiring), and the public cache constructors plus the exported capability names the library promised to keep remain reachable.
rubrics.rationale: The proxy's transaction forwarding is exactly the kind of behavior a seam re-split can silently strand (nothing in the suite pins it), and this task's consolidation wave rewired that proxy constructor, making its continued correctness a case-specific coupled obligation rather than a generic regression worry.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not relocate the merged obligation: no dependency point that previously escaped the consolidation (statement-data runner storage and its setter chain, builder factory setter records, the scan/row seam, the expression-writer path) ends up newly requesting capability families its own consumption does not reach, and no wrapper, group, or proxy declaration that survives becomes the vehicle through which the merged surface is still forced on callers.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible failure mode for an interface-narrowing task is squeezing the fat declaration out of one seam and letting it pop up in an adjacent one to keep the package compiling; this instance's seam graph (storage fields fed by reflection-style setters, group interfaces, wrapper return types) offers several such escape hatches, and each would leave the same dependency mismatch standing.

rubrics.criterion: No documentation residue from the consolidation wave survives on the re-split declarations: the removed aliases, fused-surface narration ('as part of the runner consolidation...', 'kept as a compatibility name for the unified...'), and debug-merge justification ('custom formats cannot accidentally ship without it') are deleted or rewritten so comments describe what each seam now requires, and no comment claims an interface covers capabilities its re-split declaration does not embed.
rubrics.rationale: The injection planted specific narrative doc comments telling the story of the unified surface on every declaration it fattened; leaving that story in place after a re-split leaves the library documenting a dependency boundary it no longer has, which is precisely the stale-artifact cleanup this instance must carry.

rubrics.criterion: The repair leaves no dead seam scaffolding behind: every capability declaration the repair introduces or restores is referenced by at least one dependency point (parameter, field, or assertion) in the package, and no duplicate near-identical contracts exist purely as cautionary copies of one another.
rubrics.rationale: Interface re-splits in Go tend to accumulate spare narrow contracts from incremental edits; with this case spanning four clusters across five files, unused leftovers would multiply quickly. Because they also confuse the next maintainer about which contract is the real dependency boundary, their absence is part of a finished repair.

rubrics.criterion: The capability-optional runtime behaviors keep their identity: executing with no runner configured still comes back through the RunnerNotSet error value; taking the query-row path with a runner that lacks the query-row capability still yields RunnerNotQueryRunner from that same lazy probe; and a context method probing a stored preparation target without the context capability still yields NoContextSupport rather than a type assertion panic, an incorrect fall-through, or a compile-time regime that forbids capability-partial runners entirely.
rubrics.rationale: These probes interact directly with how narrow the seam declarations are allowed to be: a repair that re-typers the probe sites or the storage must preserve the exact per-capability error semantics this package promises, and the injected consolidation already left the assertion fossilized, making this seam especially fragile.

rubrics.criterion: Placeholder behavior is preserved at both consumption points: statement rendering applies ReplacePlaceholders exactly as before for every dialect (question marks left in place, dollar/colon/@p renumbered identically, ??-escapes intact), and the debug rendering path still consults the format-specific debug token through its own private discovery rather than always falling back to a fixed placeholder or dropping the token consultation - debug output strings stay what they were.
rubrics.rationale: The debug cluster is the repair's riskiest spot because the public seam and the debug path's private probe are two different dependency points on the same implementations; a repair that removes the token method from the implementations as well as the public interface would fix the seam and silently change DebugSqlizer's rendered strings, which is a behavior change masquerading as cleanup.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not weaken the suite to fit the new seams: no existing test case is deleted or rewritten to assert weaker behavior, fake providers in tests are not re-pointed away from the package's public seams toward test-local draft declarations, and any signature-motivated test edit remains strictly mechanical (import or argument adjustments) with the case still exercising the same runtime behavior.
rubrics.rationale: A pass/fail suite re-run cannot detect coverage removed during a refactor, and interface-consolidation repairs create exactly that temptation when narrow seams expose test fixtures that were shaped for the merged one; this item keeps the deterministic green run honest for the one cheating path it cannot see.
